improvements.title: On-silicon TVLA/CPA campaign re-targeted at fors_secret and the pre-PIN tunnel crypto (first measurement ever)
improvements.threat: Every leakage claim in the repo is Unicorn mem_address Hamming weight; register-value and HASH/SAES coprocessor leakage have never been measured. Saarinen (ePrint 2024/367) hit t=24.5 at 1,000 traces on an SLH-DSA PRF; Belenky (TCHES 2023/3) forges HMAC-SHA-2 from a pure-hardware core at 30K-275K traces; pq1's 65,536-per-chain cap (bootstrap: C x 65,536) sits inside that budget, and horizontal exploitation multiplies traces per signature.
improvements.proposal: Run the first silicon campaign with hardware already on the bench (Scaffold + Rigol MHO934, red-teaming.md §13.1 recipe, sca-trigger GPIO PB3 on pq1) in this order: (a) fixed-vs-random TVLA on the fors_secret window — it is a single SHA-256 compression whose message block is sk_seed(32)||"fors"||12 known varying bytes, 26,636 calls/sign in natural leaf order, i.e. the ideal vertical-DPA shape (known varying W[8..11] added to a secret constant state in rounds 8-11); (b) TVLA on wots_secret block 2 (secret midstate chaining value + varying tree/kp/chain input); (c) CPA on the boot-time SCP03 S-ENC/S-MAC software AES (scp03_logic.rs) and the Shielded TLS-PRF HMAC (shield.rs), which an attacker can trigger unlimited times by power-cycling WITHOUT the PIN (Jade precedent); (d) SAES-CMAC(DHUK) at first-boot/page-126 unwrap. Publish the max|t| curves vs trace count in tools/sca/README.md as receipts; use them to close or escalate #228/#236 per the disposition rule already written in #228. Add a hash-counters bucket for grind_r so the secret-PRF census (70,754) stops excluding its ~2048 sk_seed-absorbing iterations.
improvements.rationale: #228 frames the measurement around the WOTS 'sk_seed-absorption window', but the code shows the WOTS first block is a per-layer CONSTANT (no varying known input, so only horizontal/template leakage) while FORS is the direct known-input DPA target — a campaign aimed at the wrong PRF would produce a false clean. The tunnel crypto is pre-PIN and unlimited-trace, so it is the cheaper attack than anything behind the 10-attempt gate. The 2025 PQC-SCA SoK (ePrint 2025/1222) records essentially no public SCA result on SHA-2 SPHINCS+ signers, so pq1 cannot cite prior art as assurance — it has to produce its own numbers, and publishing them is something neither Ledger nor Trezor does for their devices.

improvements.title: Move SE-tunnel AES (SCP03 S-ENC/S-MAC KDF + session CMAC/CBC, Shielded AES-CCM) off software AES onto SAES; add shield.rs to the leakage harness
improvements.threat: The long-term SCP03 static keys and the Shielded session keys are exercised by the bitsliced software `aes`/`cmac` crates on the CPU at EVERY boot, before any PIN, with a fixed key and attacker-known/chosen inputs — unlimited power-cycle CPA traces. Recovering S-ENC lets a bus tap decrypt half_E on the next legitimate unlock (symmetrically PBS -> half_O), defeating invariant #1 without touching either SE. Invariant #3's accepted Grover-2^64 residual silently assumes the tunnel keys are not SCA-extractable.
improvements.proposal: (a) Extend hw/saes.rs with KEYSIZE=128 (bit 18 is hard-coded to 256 at :487) and keep ECB as the only hardware mode; (b) implement CBC/CTR/CMAC for SCP03 and CCM-CTR/CBC-MAC for the Shielded Connection as software XOR/chaining over SAES ECB blocks with KeySel::Software (cmac_generic is already parameterised over a block function, cmac.rs:61), so no AES round ever runs on the CPU; (c) load the SAES-CMAC(DHUK)/BHK-derived static keys into SAES_KEYR and wipe KEYR on exit as the Tier-1 KDF already does, so the static S-ENC/S-MAC bytes have the shortest possible CPU residency; (d) the 64-B PBS TLS-PRF (HMAC-SHA256) has no SAES analogue — mitigate by running it once per power-on (not per shield re-establish), zeroizing immediately, and adding a rainbow/lascar `shield_target` (TLS-PRF, CCM tag verify, sequence window) mirroring scp03_target; (e) measure before/after with SCA-01(c).
improvements.rationale: ST documents SAES as having internal side-channel countermeasures (RNG-driven randomisation, noted at saes.rs:194 as an unmeasured hardware claim); the Tier-1 KDF already trusts it for DHUK. The SCP03 KDF and all session crypto are AES-only, so the whole SE050 tunnel can run on SAES with a small driver delta. This is the SCA counterpart of Trezor's 'hardware-keyed SAES for all PIN-derived material' and of the Jade boot-time CPA lesson. The SHSI clock and force-reset Trezor pattern is already present (saes.rs:225-244), so only the mode/keysize delta is missing.

improvements.title: WOTS PRF midstate-resume: compute the two per-layer SHA-256 midstates once per sign, resume per call (byte-identical output, no address re-base)
improvements.threat: 44,118 wots_secret calls per sign each push the raw 32-byte sk_seed through the HASH peripheral's DIN at the same intra-call offset — the horizontal/template residual of archive §18 and the exact 'SK.seed reused across thousands of PRF calls' pattern of Kannwischer 2018 / Saarinen 2024. #229 assumed closing this requires re-basing every key (invariant #6).
improvements.proposal: Because block 1 of wots_secret is sk_seed||"wots"||to_b4(layer)||tree_b32[0..24] and tree_b32[0..24] is always zero (u64 right-aligned in 32 B), the chaining value after block 1 is a constant per (sk_seed, layer). Compute the two midstates (layer 0, layer 1) once per sign (or once per SLOT_CACHE keygen) and run only block 2 per call, either (a) via the HASH peripheral's context-swap registers (HASH_CSRx suspend/resume, RM0456 §HASH 'context swapping') or (b) via `sha2::compress256` in software for the 64-byte second block with explicit padding. Outputs are bit-identical to the current `sha256(...)`, so pubkeys, CREATE2 addresses, the on-chain verifier and all test vectors are untouched; pin with a differential test against the existing wots_secret. Store the midstates as ZeroizeOnDrop in the SigningKey cache. Side effect: ~44k fewer compressions per sign (~8% of the 539,616 hashes).
improvements.rationale: Reduces sk_seed-absorbing compressions from 44,118+26,636 to 26,636 (FORS only) + 2 without any wire/derivation change, closing the WOTS half of #229 pre- AND post-launch. Honest limit: block-2 compressions still combine a secret chaining value with varying known input, so the vertical-DPA exposure on the midstate (which suffices to forge WOTS for that layer; layer-1 WOTS alone is a full forgery) is UNCHANGED — this item removes the horizontal/template surface on sk_seed itself, which is the key shared with FORS and grind_r. FORS cannot be restructured this way (single block, secret and varying input mixed).

improvements.title: Arm the ADC4 analog watchdogs so ITAMP7/12/13 actually fire (in-silicon voltage-glitch / temperature / rail-manipulation detector feeding tamp-wipe)
improvements.threat: SCA and FI attackers lower/raise VDD, cool/heat the die and inject rail glitches to raise leakage or skip checks (Masaryk thesis ~76% PIN-glitch bypass on STM32U5; Donjon t-test-guided double LFI on Coldcard SE2). pq1 has no analog monitor of its own supply: the three ADC4-watchdog tamper enables are set but ADC4 is never configured, so they can never trigger.
improvements.proposal: Configure ADC4 (low-power ADC in the SRD domain) in continuous/injected mode on the internal channels VREFINT, VCORE and the temperature sensor, set AWD1/AWD2/AWD3 windows from factory-characterised values (per-die calibration stored on page 127 at first boot alongside the salt), route the AWD events to ITAMP7/12/13 (already enabled, tamp.rs:288-299) so a confirmed excursion zeroizes the BHK backup registers and triggers the existing tzic intrusion wipe. Ship in two stages: (1) log-only with a page-127 excursion counter and bench characterisation on EVT (voltage sweep, thermal chamber) to set thresholds; (2) `tamp-wipe` escalation once false-positive rate is measured. Secure ADC4 in GTZC (it is in GTZC2/SRD, the same open follow-up as TAMP).
improvements.rationale: It is the only on-die signal that the attacker is operating outside nominal conditions, it costs no board change, and it turns three already-enabled-but-dormant tamper bits into a real detector. ST intends exactly this use (RM0456 TAMP: 'ADC4 analog watchdog monitoring 1/2/3'). Both Trezor and pq1 currently enable the flags without the ADC — so this is beyond both.

improvements.title: Always-on secure-timer random-delay interrupt (RDI) with a TRNG-reseeded DRBG and per-NSC-entry session refresh — after resolving #835
improvements.threat: C10 signing is ~7 s of highly repetitive secret-dependent SHA-256 that aligns trivially across traces; wait_random() only perturbs annotated sites (PIN gate, sign gates), so the 70k PRF calls inside a sign run on a deterministic timeline relative to the sca-trigger/USB event. Trace alignment is the enabling step for every horizontal and vertical attack in SCA-01.
improvements.proposal: Port Trezor's RDI as a 1 ms ISR on the already-secured TIM2 (sau.rs secures TIM2/TIM3 so NS cannot stop it): wait(fresh U[0,255] + session U[0,255]) with the exact-cycle asm loop, session term refreshed on every NSC dispatch entry/exit (the pq1 analogue of smcall/USB events). Feed it from a SP 800-90A-shaped ChaCha-DRBG seeded from the platform TRNG (register read only, never rng_strong — the sca-1 owner rule), reseeded every N calls, consumed bytes zeroized, with the #832 pre-drawn pool replacing the #833/#834 halt sink that #835 found net-negative. The ISR must never touch SE I2C and must be masked around the T=1'/IFX-I2C guard-time-critical windows.
improvements.rationale: Issue #805 already makes the case and the earlier 'category error' rejection (2026-06-30) is superseded by its new measurements; Trezor runs it everywhere for ~0.2% CPU. It is the cheapest broad-spectrum desync available and the only one that covers the FORS/WOTS inner loops without touching sphincs-c10. The FI delay source has had three defects in a month (#643/#832/#835) — building the RDI on the same pool forces that source to be fixed properly first.

improvements.title: Device-bound PIN whitening via SAES-CMAC(DHUK) before presentation to either SE (digest-before-send), replacing the raw 8-byte PIN on the SE050 path and the software SHA-256 on the OPTIGA path
improvements.threat: The raw PIN is sent to SE050 inside SCP03 (se050/mod.rs:3025 unlock(pin: &[u8;8])), and the OPTIGA path hashes the 8-digit PIN on the CPU with software SHA-256 once per attempt (optiga/mod.rs:916-918). Under invariant #3's accepted Grover-2^64 bus residual the plaintext an attacker recovers is the PIN itself; and a single-trace template/SPA attack on one SHA-256 over a ~27-bit input learns typed digits even on a WRONG-PIN trace (Donjon Trezor-One PIN attack class), bypassing the 10-attempt bound.
improvements.proposal: Pre-launch (CLAUDE.md allows re-provisioning): present to each SE a per-SE, device-bound digest d_X = SAES-CMAC(DHUK, label_X || PIN || salt) (Tier-1 KDF already exists, secret_keys.rs derive_into_saes_kdf) instead of the PIN: SE050 UserID value = d_E (16 B), OPTIGA AuthRef secret = d_O. The PIN bytes then never meet software SHA-256 or the I2C bus; a tapped tunnel yields a value useless without the die; each SE sees a different digest so a leaky SE reveals nothing about the other. Keep invariant #2 intact (the compare stays in SE silicon); update the first-boot wizard, duress-PIN and admin-wipe provisioning to use the same transform. Optionally fold the PIN into SAES via DHUK^BHK so it is bound to the BHK too (Trezor XORK pattern).
improvements.rationale: Trezor stretches on the MCU (PBKDF2 x20000 + device salt) and then SAES-whitens before anything reaches the Optiga/Tropic, and its docs state the rationale: a compromised link or malicious SE cannot reduce security below 'no SE'. pq1 has the stronger SE-side compare but the weaker transport story. Using SAES-CMAC(DHUK) instead of PBKDF2 keeps the transform on the DPA-hardened block and avoids a long software hash on a low-entropy input.

improvements.title: Consumption mask: GPDMA-fed TRNG sample table, a real load on the mask pin, and a measured dilution figure (close #831/#646 on the way)
improvements.threat: The production fence forces the mask on, yet neither board drives a load from the mask pin (pq1 PA6 is NC), the duty is stepped by the CPU once per SysTick from an xorshift32 whose reseed fails open and is biased away from signing windows (#831) — so the only CPA/DPA noise source the firmware claims is unmeasured and physically doubtful.
improvements.proposal: (a) Hardware (EVT): populate a load on PA6 (series resistor to GND sized for a few mA, or tie the TIM3_CH1 output to the existing backlight/LED driver enable) so duty changes actually modulate die/rail current; (b) firmware: port Trezor's GPDMA circular linked-list (119 TRNG samples, secure+privileged channel, TIM3_UP request -> CCR1) so the mask pattern changes at ~10 kHz with zero CPU involvement and is uncorrelated with code; refill the table from the TRNG at sign start/end and per display refresh; make the reseed fail-closed with a counter (the #831 fix); (c) measure: capture a sign with the mask off vs on (Rigol, §13.1) and report SNR/t-statistic reduction in evt-silicon-validation.md §9 — convert 'satisfied-by-construction' into a number.
improvements.rationale: Trezor's DMA design decouples the mask from firmware activity; pq1's SysTick-stepped design is correlated with the 1 ms cadence and gives ~1 kHz of entropy. More importantly nobody has measured either vendor's mask, so a measured figure is a differentiator. If the measurement shows no dilution, the honest outcome is to stop presenting the mask as a load-bearing CPA/DPA defence (README.md:233 vs nsc/mod.rs fence text disagree today).

improvements.title: Exponential on-device back-off before every PIN attempt (S-only timer, cancellable), ahead of the counter precharge
improvements.threat: Automated SCA/FI campaigns against the unlock sequence (profiled PIN-digit recovery on wrong-PIN traces, glitch sweeps on gated_unlock, template attacks on the page-124 precharge) run at the natural ~5 s unlock cadence; the only brake is the 10-attempt wipe, which a glitch campaign is specifically trying to bypass.
improvements.proposal: Add get_backoff_ms = (2^fails - 1) * 1000 using the page-124 used-count (already read at boot/unlock) and busy-wait it on the S-only TIM (the same timer discipline as the inactivity timeout, so NS cannot shorten it) BEFORE the page-124 precharge and SE call, with the trusted-UI showing a countdown the user can cancel (cancel = no attempt consumed). Apply the same wait before the PendSV re-unlock retry so a persistent SE fault (#692) cannot burn the budget quickly.
improvements.rationale: Trezor ships exactly this (storage.c:1158-1207); it costs nothing, is S-world only, and multiplies the wall-clock cost of every wrong-attempt trace, which is the unit of work for both the Donjon PIN-SCA and the Masaryk PIN-glitch classes. pq1's lockout is purely count-based today.

improvements.title: Additive-random-masked secret compares for the MCU-side master cross-check and PIN-confirm (Trezor secequal32 parity)
improvements.threat: subtle::ct_eq is constant-TIME but the Hamming weight of (derived XOR stored) still modulates power while the two 32-byte secrets are compared; dual_se.rs runs that compare twice per unlock (both operands secret: derived_master vs on-chip stored master), and pin_entry's XOR-OR confirm compares two secret PIN buffers. A profiled attacker gets one such trace per unlock.
improvements.proposal: Add `ct_eq_masked32(a, b)` to pqsigner-fi: per 32-bit word draw a fresh mask m from the pre-drawn TRNG pool and accumulate diff |= ((a + m) - b) ^ m, with the loop-completion FI check (i == wn), returning a Hamming-distant sentinel; use it at dual_se.rs:305-310 (both compares) and in pin_entry's confirm fold. Keep subtle::ct_eq for public-vs-public compares (the 4008-B double-compute signature compare is public output and does not need masking).
improvements.rationale: Low-cost, verified Trezor construction (storage.c:220-243, re-read this session) that hides operand Hamming weights during the compare; pq1's fi helpers already have the sentinel and loop-completion idioms, so it is a drop-in. Complements SCA-01: a masked compare is the kind of change whose effect a TVLA can confirm.

improvements.title: Secret-frame emanation hardening on the NV3007 SPI path: per-render pixel/backlight randomisation after atlas verification, LCD decoy re-test, and the #784 bypass fix
improvements.threat: The LCD MOSI line carries plaintext pixel data on a periodic TE-synced refresh and ui-px renders from a fixed SHA-256-pinned glyph atlas — the cached-glyph anti-pattern Kuhn showed 'merely assists the eavesdropper' (readable text at 3-10 m from an FPD link by frame averaging). Backlight/panel current also correlates with lit pixels (CVE-2019-14354 class, recurred on Ledger's non-SSD1306 panel in 2023). F-24's decoy-frames mitigation was validated only on the removed OLED; the restore wizard renders seed letters on a non-forced frame (#784).
improvements.proposal: (a) Fix #784 so every secret glyph goes through the CT blitter/force path; (b) in the compositor, AFTER the atlas hash check, randomise the low-order colour bits of every pixel of a secret frame and the row/strip write order per render (fresh TRNG per frame, so frame averaging no longer converges), keeping the rendered intent identical; (c) randomise backlight PWM phase/duty within a visually invisible band during secret frames (Ledger's 'randomized screen-update parameters' analogue); (d) re-run the F-24 decoy/TVLA experiment on the real NV3007 panel with the §13.1 rig and record the result in tools/sca/README.md (replacing the stale SSD1306 section); (e) keep secret frames on screen for the minimum time and prefer never-display backup flows where the UX allows.
improvements.rationale: This is the one SCA window where the secret is the seed itself (wizard) or the PIN, and the one with a real-world implant precedent (Grand's Nano X SPI tap). Randomisation must sit after atlas verification so the WYSIWYS pin stays intact. The repo already has the CT blitter (lcd.rs:196) — the missing delta is per-render entropy, the LCD re-test, and closing the bypass.
